differences.title: 1. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB uses C++ and shared-nothing architecture with an event-loop model for significantly lower latency and higher throughput, especially for write-heavy workloads.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra offers robust, scalable performance across distributed nodes, optimized for high availability and fault tolerance, with tunable consistency for reads and writes.

differences.title: 2. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB's C++ rewrite focuses on a shared-nothing, shard-per-core model for maximum hardware utilization and parallelism, reducing contention and garbage collection overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra employs a distributed, peer-to-peer architecture where all nodes are equal, simplifying cluster management and ensuring no single point of failure.

differences.title: 3. PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB's C++ implementation allows for fine-grained memory management and direct hardware interaction, leading to predictable performance and reduced GC pauses.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra's Java foundation provides a mature ecosystem and portability, though JVM tuning and GC can sometimes impact latency consistency.

differences.title: 4. OPERATIONAL OVERHEAD
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB's efficient C++ code and intelligent resource management result in a smaller memory footprint and less CPU overhead per node.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra, being Java-based, typically requires more memory and CPU resources per node due to the JVM and its garbage collection mechanisms.

differences.title: 5. CONSISTENCY TUNING
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB offers granular consistency levels, allowing developers to balance read/write performance with data accuracy on a per-operation basis.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra provides tunable consistency with options like ONE, QUORUM, and ALL, enabling trade-offs between availability and data consistency.

differences.title: 6. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB's community is vibrant and rapidly expanding, with active development and increasing adoption, backed by strong commercial support.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra boasts a large, mature ecosystem and a vast community, benefiting from years of development, numerous integrations, and widespread industry trust.

differences.title: 7. COMPATIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: ScyllaDB is designed for drop-in compatibility with Apache Cassandra, allowing easy migration and use of existing Cassandra tools and drivers.
differences.rightDesc: Cassandra's native implementation of CQL (Cassandra Query Language) is its primary interface, offering a familiar SQL-like experience.
